articles/api-authentication.html.title: API Authentication | Organizor
articles/api-authentication.html.summary: API Authentication Overview This document explains how the Organizor API authenticates requests using Keycloak-issued JWT tokens. JWT Validation The API validates tokens using the Keycloak realm: Authority: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Audience validation: disabled for the current development setup Token type: Bearer The authentication middleware: validates the token signature; validates the issuer; validates token expiration; populates HttpContext.User. Audience validation is intentionally disabled in code while the Keycloak client and token shape are still being finalized. Once the API has a stable audience claim, enable audience validation and document the expected value here. Authentication Flow Frontend logs in via Keycloak. Keycloak issues a JWT. Frontend sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. Frontend also sends X-Tenant-Slug: acme for tenant-scoped routes. API validates the JWT. [Authorize] attributes enforce authentication where applied. Service Accounts The organizor-api client can use the client_credentials flow for internal API-to-API communication. Service account tokens are identified by the client_id claim: "client_id": "organizor-api" Service accounts bypass tenant access checks. WhoAmI Endpoint Example response: { "user": "admin@acme.dev", "tenant": null, "tenantClaims": [ "/tenants/acme/admins" ], "roles": [ "tenant-admin", "tenant-user" ], "claims": [ { "type": "sub", "value": "..." }, { "type": "tenant", "value": "/tenants/acme/admins" }, { "type": "role", "value": "tenant-admin" } ] } Error Codes 401 Unauthorized -> Missing or invalid token. 403 Forbidden -> Token is valid, but the user is not allowed. 400 Bad Request -> Missing or invalid tenant header on tenant-scoped routes. Test Request GET https://localhost:7184/api/auth/whoami Authorization: Bearer <token>

articles/api-integration.html.title: API Integration — Portal UI | Organizor
articles/api-integration.html.summary: API Integration — Portal UI The Portal UI communicates with the Organizor API through named HTTP clients. Authenticated backend calls use the api client. Anonymous public registration uses the public-api client without the authorization message handler. Local Development Configuration Setting Value Portal origin https://localhost:7025 API base URL https://localhost:7184 Authorized API URL https://localhost:7184 Token issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Portal OIDC client organizor-ui The portal and API must agree on the Keycloak issuer. If the portal logs in through HTTPS but the API validates against the old HTTP authority, API requests fail with 401 Unauthorized. HttpClient Registration The portal registers the API client in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddHttpClient("api", client => { client.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://localhost:7184"); }) .AddHttpMessageHandler<ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler>(); AdminTenantService, TenantUserService, and TenantConfigService use IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient("api") to call authenticated API endpoints. Authorization Handler ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler extends Blazor's AuthorizationMessageHandler. It is responsible for: configuring the authorized API URL; requesting the portal OIDC scopes; attaching the access token to outgoing API requests; adding the X-Tenant-Slug header when a tenant claim is available. The handler is registered in DI and configured once in its constructor. This matters because AuthorizationMessageHandler.ConfigureHandler(...) can only be called once per handler instance. Calling ConfigureHandler(...) again for the same handler instance can cause this runtime error: handler already configured Keep handler configuration inside the handler constructor or inside the AddHttpMessageHandler factory, but not both. The current branch uses the constructor approach. Tenant Admin API Client AdminTenantService wraps the admin tenant API surface used by /admin/tenants and /admin/plans. Tenant query, lifecycle, effective config, override, and plan-management endpoints require the Organizor admin policy. Method Endpoint Purpose GetTenantsAsync GET /api/admin/tenants Loads all tenants, including soft-deleted records. OnboardAsync POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Creates the catalog tenant, provisions Keycloak resources, creates the database, and applies migrations. UpgradeAsync POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Runs pending migrations for the tenant database. SoftDeleteAsync DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Marks a tenant as deleted without dropping the database. HardDeleteAsync POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Drops the tenant database and removes the catalog record after soft deletion. GetConfigAsync GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Loads the tenant's effective config after plan defaults and overrides are resolved. GetConfigOverridesAsync GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Loads explicit tenant-level config overrides. UpdateConfigOverridesAsync PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Updates tenant-level config overrides. GetPlansAsync GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Loads tenant plan defaults. UpdatePlanAsync PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Updates tenant plan defaults. tenant user methods /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/users/* Manage users for a selected tenant from the platform control plane. The backend also exposes GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} for admin detail lookups. The current portal grid does not call that endpoint directly. All methods expect an authenticated organizor-admin user. 401 Unauthorized means the token is missing or invalid. 403 Forbidden means the token is valid but lacks the required role. Tenant query responses include lifecycle fields that the portal relies on: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme", "createdAt": "2026-06-09T10:30:00Z", "status": "Active", "failureReason": null, "isDeleted": false } GET /api/v1/tenants returns only non-deleted catalog records. GET /api/admin/tenants intentionally includes soft-deleted records so the portal can show deleted tenants and allow hard deletion. Tenant User API Client TenantUserService wraps tenant-scoped user-management endpoints used by /tenant/users. These requests require a bearer token with tenant-admin and the X-Tenant-Slug header. ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler adds the tenant header when the authenticated user has a tenant claim. Tenant admins can create users, list users, toggle enabled state, assign tenant roles, and delete users inside their own tenant. Regular tenant-user accounts do not get this portal route. Tenant Config API Client TenantConfigService wraps the tenant-scoped config endpoint used by tenant admins at /tenant/config. Method Endpoint Purpose GetConfigAsync GET /api/v1/tenant/config Loads the current tenant's effective config. The request must include a bearer token with tenant-admin and the X-Tenant-Slug header. ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler adds the tenant header when the authenticated user has a tenant claim. Static Tenant Website API Contract Tenant-specific static websites should first call: GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth The response contains the tenant's website base URL, public Keycloak authority, generated client id, PKCE requirement, scopes, redirect metadata, tenant header name, tenant claim name, expected tenant roles, expected tenant group paths, and public registration endpoint. This endpoint intentionally returns no secrets. After login, static tenant websites must send Authorization: Bearer <token> and X-Tenant-Slug: {slug} on tenant-scoped authenticated API calls. Public Registration API Client PublicRegistrationService wraps POST /api/public/register for the temporary /register shell. It uses the named public-api client instead of the authenticated api client because registration is anonymous and the tenant slug is supplied in the request body. The future tenant-specific static websites should reuse the same public registration contract with their own UI. Error Handling The tenant API client uses EnsureSuccessAsync to surface failed API responses as InvalidOperationException. The exception message includes the status code and response body when present. The Radzen tenant page catches those exceptions and displays both a page alert and a Radzen notification. Troubleshooting Symptom Likely cause Fix handler already configured The same AuthorizationMessageHandler instance was configured more than once. Configure the handler in one place only. The current branch configures it in ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler's constructor. 401 Unauthorized while logged in API Keycloak:Authority does not match the token issuer, or no access token was attached. Align API authority with https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev and verify the named API client uses the auth handler. 403 Forbidden while logged in The token is valid but does not include organizor-admin. Assign the role in Keycloak and log in again to get a fresh token. Tenant-scoped API returns bad tenant errors Tenant header is missing or invalid. Verify the user has a tenant claim and ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler adds the header for tenant-scoped endpoints.

articles/api.html.title: Public API Behavior | Organizor
articles/api.html.summary: Public API Behavior The public API exposes tenant catalog endpoints, tenant-scoped config reads, anonymous tenant-user self-registration, and static tenant website authentication discovery. Tenant catalog endpoints are platform/catalog routes, so tenant resolution does not require X-Tenant-Slug for them. They are still authenticated: POST /api/v1/tenants requires organizor-admin. GET /api/v1/tenants and GET /api/v1/tenants/{slug} require organizor-admin, tenant-admin, or tenant-user. Tenant-scoped application endpoints, including GET /api/v1/tenant/config and tenant user-management routes, must include the X-Tenant-Slug header unless the path is explicitly skipped by tenant resolution. Internal tenant administration endpoints are documented separately in Internal Operations. Static Tenant Website Auth Contract GET /api/public/tenants/acme/auth Accept: application/json Returns the public OIDC settings a tenant-specific static website needs before login. The endpoint is anonymous and only returns data for active, non-deleted tenants. Example response: { "tenantSlug": "acme", "authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev", "clientId": "tenant-acme-web", "websiteBaseUrl": "https://acme.example.com", "responseType": "code", "usePkce": true, "tenantHeaderName": "X-Tenant-Slug", "tenantClaimName": "tenant", "tenantUserRole": "tenant-user", "tenantAdminRole": "tenant-admin", "tenantUserGroupPath": "/tenants/acme/users", "tenantAdminGroupPath": "/tenants/acme/admins", "scopes": ["openid", "profile", "email"], "loginRedirectUris": [ "https://acme.example.com/authentication/login-callback" ], "logoutRedirectUris": [ "https://acme.example.com" ], "webOrigins": [ "https://acme.example.com" ], "registrationRedirectUrl": "https://acme.example.com/register/complete", "publicRegistrationEndpoint": "/api/public/register" } Static tenant websites should use this contract to: configure OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE; link back to the tenant website using websiteBaseUrl; use the generated tenant client id; request openid profile email; send X-Tenant-Slug: {tenantSlug} on tenant-scoped authenticated API calls; expect the Keycloak token to contain a tenant claim from the tenant-membership mapper. expect user tokens to be members of /tenants/{tenantSlug}/users or /tenants/{tenantSlug}/admins and to carry the matching tenant-user or tenant-admin role required by the target endpoint. Possible responses: Status Meaning 200 OK Contract returned for an active tenant. 400 Bad Request Tenant slug or stored auth settings are invalid. 404 Not Found Tenant does not exist, is deleted, or is not active. Public Tenant User Registration POST /api/public/register Content-Type: application/json { "tenantSlug": "acme", "username": "jane.doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "password": "correct-horse-battery-staple" } Creates an enabled tenant-user account for an active tenant. This endpoint is anonymous and does not use X-Tenant-Slug; the tenant is selected from the request body. Registration uses Keycloak as the source of truth and assigns the user to /tenants/{slug}/users. The API validates the tenant exists, is active, has effective settings.registration.enabled set to boolean true, and has not reached its configured user limit. The portal /register page is only a temporary shell for testing this feature. Future tenant-specific static websites should provide their own UI and call this API contract directly. Possible responses: Status Meaning 200 OK User was created and assigned to the tenant user group. 400 Bad Request Request validation failed, effective registration config is invalid, or registration is disabled. 404 Not Found Tenant slug does not resolve to an active tenant. 409 Conflict Username or email already exists in Keycloak, or the tenant user limit was reached. 502 Bad Gateway Keycloak rejected the user operation or could not complete it. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server error. See Errors and Observability. Tenant Catalog Create Tenant POST /api/v1/tenants Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme" } Creates a catalog tenant record with Pending status and returns tenant metadata. This route does not provision Keycloak groups, a default tenant admin, or a tenant database. Use POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard for the full onboarding workflow. Example response: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme", "createdAt": "2026-06-09T10:30:00Z", "status": "Pending", "failureReason": null, "isDeleted": false } All tenant catalog responses use the same shape: Field Meaning id Tenant catalog identifier. name Human-readable tenant name. slug Stable slug used for lookup and tenant routing. databaseName Tenant database name assigned by the catalog. createdAt UTC catalog creation timestamp. status Current lifecycle status, such as Pending, Active, Failed, or Deleted. failureReason Provisioning or lifecycle failure detail when available. isDeleted Whether the catalog record has been soft-deleted. Public reads exclude deleted records. Possible responses: Status Meaning 200 OK Tenant catalog record was created. 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid bearer token. 403 Forbidden Token does not satisfy the organizor-admin role policy. 409 Conflict Duplicate tenant slug. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server error. See Errors and Observability. Get Tenant By Slug GET /api/v1/tenants/acme Authorization: Bearer <token> Returns a tenant by slug using the tenant catalog response shape above, or 404 Not Found when no tenant exists. Soft-deleted tenants are excluded. List Tenants GET /api/v1/tenants Authorization: Bearer <token> Returns all catalog tenants visible through the tenant repository using the tenant catalog response shape above. Soft-deleted tenants are excluded. Tenant Config GET /api/v1/tenant/config Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Returns the current tenant's effective config. Effective config is resolved from the tenant's assigned plan defaults plus tenant-specific overrides. This endpoint requires organizor-admin or tenant-admin through the RequireTenantAdminRole policy. Tenant access middleware also verifies that the authenticated user belongs to the tenant identified by X-Tenant-Slug. Platform Endpoints Endpoint Purpose /health Public health check endpoint. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer in development. OpenAPI And Scalar When the API runs in development: OpenAPI JSON is available at /openapi/v1.json. Scalar is available at /scalar. Use this article for behavior: routes, authorization expectations, tenant headers, response shapes, and operational meaning. Use the generated API reference only for C# type signatures.

articles/architecture.html.title: Architecture | Organizor
articles/architecture.html.summary: Architecture Organizor follows a layered structure around tenant management. flowchart LR Client[HTTP client] --> Api[Code7Dev.Organizor.Api] Api --> Application[Code7Dev.Organizor.Application] Application --> Domain[Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain] Application --> Infrastructure[Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure] Api --> Quartz[Quartz scheduler] Quartz --> Infrastructure Infrastructure --> Catalog[(Catalog database)] Infrastructure --> TenantDb[(Tenant databases)] API Layer The API project owns transport concerns: controller routes for public tenant catalog operations and internal tenant operations; request and response DTOs; mapping between API DTOs and application models; correlation ID, exception handling, and tenant resolution middleware; Serilog request logging; CORS, health checks, OpenAPI, and Scalar setup. The startup flow in Program.cs composes the application by registering catalog persistence, tenant persistence, application services, infrastructure services, and API services. Application Layer The application project owns use cases and contracts. It defines interfaces for repository access, tenant database management, migration, provisioning, onboarding, upgrades, lifecycle operations, tenant config resolution, config overrides, and plan management. Current services: Service Responsibility TenantService Creates catalog tenant records and reads tenants by slug or as a list. TenantOnboardingService Creates a catalog tenant, runs provisioning, and marks the tenant active or failed. TenantLifecycleService Soft-deletes tenants and hard-deletes already soft-deleted tenants. TenantUpgradeService Runs migrations for an existing tenant database. TenantConfigResolver Resolves effective tenant config from plan defaults plus tenant overrides. TenantConfigManagementService Reads and updates tenant-specific config overrides. TenantPlanManagementService Reads and updates tenant plan defaults. Domain Layer The domain project contains the tenant entity, tenant plan entity, tenant feature-settings value object, and tenant status enum. A tenant stores identity, slug, database name, plan key, config overrides, creation date, lifecycle status, provisioning failure reason, and deletion metadata. Tenant plans store reusable defaults for feature limits and behavior. Infrastructure Layer The infrastructure project owns external resources: CatalogDbContext stores tenant records. OrganizorDbContext connects to the current tenant database after tenant resolution. TenantRepository implements catalog tenant persistence. TenantPlanRepository implements tenant plan persistence. ConnectionStringBuilder builds PostgreSQL connection strings from configuration. TenantDatabaseManager creates and drops tenant databases. TenantMigrator applies EF Core migrations to tenant databases. TenantProvisioningWorkflow creates a tenant database and applies migrations during onboarding. TenantJobScheduler schedules tenant-scoped Quartz jobs from catalog tenant records. TenantAwareJobFactory creates Quartz jobs through dependency injection. SyncTenantJob runs recurring tenant synchronization work with ITenantContext populated from Quartz job data. Background Jobs Quartz is registered by the API layer and backed by persistent PostgreSQL storage in the catalog database. On startup, the application schedules a recurring synchronization job for each catalog tenant. Each job carries the tenant ID and slug in Quartz job data, then sets the tenant context before running tenant database work. Request Pipeline sequenceDiagram participant Client participant Api participant TenantResolution participant Application participant Infrastructure Client->>Api: HTTP request Api->>Api: Correlation ID and exception handling Api->>TenantResolution: Resolve tenant when required TenantResolution->>Infrastructure: Load tenant by X-Tenant-Slug Infrastructure-->>TenantResolution: Tenant record TenantResolution->>Application: Continue with current tenant context Application->>Infrastructure: Use catalog or tenant database services Infrastructure-->>Application: Result Application-->>Api: Model Api-->>Client: HTTP response

articles/authentication-flow.html.title: Authentication Flow — Portal UI | Organizor
articles/authentication-flow.html.summary: Authentication Flow — Portal UI The Portal UI uses Keycloak to authenticate users and determine which shell they should see. The process follows OpenID Connect Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Login Flow The user clicks Login or navigates to a protected route. The Portal redirects to Keycloak at https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. Keycloak validates the credentials. Keycloak redirects back to https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback. Blazor WebAssembly stores the authenticated state and access token. KeycloakClaimsPrincipalFactory maps Keycloak roles into Blazor role claims. RoleRedirector sends the user to the correct shell when they return from the neutral entry routes. Role Redirects RoleRedirector currently routes users as follows: Role Redirect target organizor-admin /admin tenant-admin /tenant tenant-user /tenant/profile The redirector must only redirect from neutral routes such as / and authentication/login-callback. It should not force navigation when the user is already on /admin or /tenant, because forced self-navigation can create a reload loop. Logout is initiated either by LogoutButton or the /logout route. Both call Blazor WebAssembly authentication through NavigateToLogout("authentication/logout", "/"), which clears the local authentication state and returns the browser to / after the identity-provider logout flow. Role Claims in the Portal The portal role factory reads roles from Keycloak claims and adds ClaimTypes.Role entries for Blazor authorization. Supported sources: realm_access.roles resource_access.organizor-ui.roles This is separate from API role mapping, where the API also understands roles under resource_access.organizor-api.roles. The portal claims factory also promotes custom tenant and groups values when Keycloak returns them as token properties. Tenant onboarding ensures the organizor-ui client has the group-membership mapper needed to emit the tenant claim from /tenants/{slug}/... group membership. Protected Routes Portal pages use role attributes: @attribute [Authorize(Roles = "organizor-admin")] Current route protection: Route area Required role /admin organizor-admin /admin/tenants organizor-admin /admin/plans organizor-admin /admin/users organizor-admin /tenant tenant-admin /tenant/users tenant-admin /tenant/config tenant-admin /tenant/profile tenant-admin, tenant-user /register anonymous Tenant users are redirected to their profile because regular users should not see tenant platform configuration. Tenant admins can still open their profile from the tenant shell. API Tokens The Portal never sends credentials to the API. It sends bearer tokens through the configured API HttpClient. The API validates token signature, issuer, expiration, and then applies authorization policies. The local issuer must be consistent everywhere: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev If the API is configured with http://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev, it will reject HTTPS-issued portal tokens with 401 Unauthorized. Keycloak Client Requirements The organizor-ui client must allow: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7025/* Web origin https://localhost:7025 Flow Standard flow / Authorization Code with PKCE Users must receive the appropriate Organizor role before logging in. If roles are changed in Keycloak, log out and back in to refresh the token and claims. The current-user display reads these claims when present: Claim Use preferred_username Display name fallback before email. email User contact display. tenant Tenant context and X-Tenant-Slug header source. name, given_name, family_name Profile display fields when provided by Keycloak. role claims Sidebar and profile access display. groups Sidebar user context display. Current-User Account Actions The tenant profile page does not link tenant users or tenant admins directly to the Keycloak account console. Password and profile actions use an Organizor-mediated flow: the client calls a tenant-scoped API endpoint, the API validates the authenticated user and tenant access, and Keycloak completes the required action. Password-change initiation is exposed as POST /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/change-password and sets Keycloak UPDATE_PASSWORD for the authenticated user. Organizor must not collect, store, or log replacement passwords. Profile update is exposed as PUT /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/profile and updates only Keycloak firstName and lastName for the authenticated user. Username, email, tenant membership, groups, roles, credentials, enabled state, required actions, and arbitrary attributes are not editable through this current-user profile endpoint. Broader Keycloak UPDATE_PROFILE flows remain deferred until user-profile policy is specified.

articles/component-structure.html.title: Portal UI Structure — High-Level | Organizor
articles/component-structure.html.summary: Portal UI Structure — High-Level The Portal UI is organized into pages, layouts, components, services, and models. Pages Page Route Responsibility Home / Neutral entry page. Authenticated users can be redirected by role. Authentication /authentication/* Blazor WebAssembly OIDC login/logout callbacks. Logout /logout Convenience route that starts Blazor OIDC logout and returns to /. Admin/Dashboard /admin Admin dashboard placeholder. Admin/Tenants /admin/tenants Operational tenant catalog and lifecycle management. Admin/Plans /admin/plans Tenant plan default management. Admin/Users /admin/users?tenantId={id} Platform control-plane user management for one active tenant. TenantAdmin/Dashboard /tenant Tenant dashboard placeholder. TenantAdmin/Users /tenant/users Tenant-scoped user management. TenantAdmin/Config /tenant/config Tenant-admin effective tenant configuration. TenantShared/Profile /tenant/profile Shared read-only profile for tenant admins and tenant users. Register /register Temporary public self-registration shell. NotFound fallback Not-found page. Tenant-admin-only pages live under Pages/TenantAdmin. Shared tenant pages live under Pages/TenantShared. This keeps future tenant-user-specific pages separate from tenant platform administration. Layouts Layout Responsibility MainLayout General shell with login/logout controls and authenticated user context. AdminLayout Admin control-plane shell with dashboard, tenant management, plan management, current-user panel, logout, and tenant website navigation when available. TenantLayout Tenant shell with role-aware tenant navigation, current-user panel, logout, and public-site navigation. Components Component Responsibility UserInfo Displays tenant, username, email, and Keycloak groups from the current authentication state. CurrentUserPanel Sidebar user card used in admin and tenant shells. Shows display name, email, tenant, groups, logout, and tenant website navigation when available. LogoutButton Starts Blazor OIDC logout through NavigateToLogout("authentication/logout", "/"). RoleRedirector Redirects authenticated users from neutral entry routes to /admin, /tenant, or /tenant/profile based on role. RedirectToLogin Sends unauthenticated users to the Blazor OIDC login route. AuthStateProvider Auth-related component wrapper used by the portal. AdminSidebar Admin navigation component retained for admin navigation reuse. UserCreateForm Shared user-create form used by platform and tenant user-management pages. UserGrid Shared user grid used by platform and tenant user-management pages. Radzen Usage The portal references Radzen.Blazor and wires RadzenComponents in App.razor. The admin tenant page currently uses: RadzenDataGrid for tenant catalog display; RadzenTemplateForm, RadzenTextBox, RadzenTextArea, and validators for tenant onboarding and deletion input; RadzenCard for layout panels; RadzenButton for actions; RadzenBadge for tenant status; RadzenAlert and NotificationService for errors and operation feedback. Radzen services registered in Program.cs: DialogService NotificationService TooltipService ContextMenuService Services Service Responsibility UserContextService Reads AuthenticationState and maps claims into UserInfoModel. ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler Attaches access tokens to API requests and adds tenant header context when available. AdminTenantService Typed client for admin tenant, plan, config inspection, override, and platform user-management operations. TenantUserService Typed client for tenant-scoped user-management operations used by /tenant/users. TenantConfigService Typed client for the tenant-scoped effective config endpoint used by tenant admins at /tenant/config. PublicRegistrationService Typed client for anonymous tenant-user self-registration from /register. PublicTenantAuthService Typed client for anonymous tenant auth discovery used to resolve the tenant website link. KeycloakClaimsPrincipalFactory Promotes Keycloak roles into Blazor role claims. Models Model Purpose UserInfoModel Display model for signed-in user context. TenantModel Portal-side tenant catalog projection. TenantOnboardingForm Validated form model for tenant onboarding. TenantOnboardingRequest API request body for onboarding. TenantSoftDeleteRequest API request body for soft deletion. TenantMigrationResult API response model for tenant database upgrades. TenantEffectiveConfigModel Effective tenant config response model used by tenant and admin config views. TenantPlanModel Tenant plan defaults model used by /admin/plans. TenantConfigOverridesModel Tenant plan assignment and override model used by /admin/tenants. TenantUserModel Portal-side Keycloak tenant-user projection. TenantUserRegistrationForm Public registration form model used by /register. TenantModel mirrors the API tenant response used by the admin grid: Id, Name, Slug, DatabaseName, CreatedAt, Status, FailureReason, and IsDeleted. Extension Rules Add page-level authorization attributes to protected pages. Keep API calls inside services instead of Razor markup. Use the named api HttpClient for backend calls so tokens are attached consistently. Avoid forcing full page reloads for internal route redirects unless a complete browser reload is required. Do not add UI for operations until the backing API route exists, unless the page is clearly marked as a placeholder.

articles/configuration.html.title: Configuration | Organizor
articles/configuration.html.summary: Configuration Organizor reads standard ASP.NET Core configuration from appsettings.json, environment-specific files, user secrets, and environment variables. Catalog Connection String CatalogDbContext expects a connection string named Catalog. Example shape: { "ConnectionStrings": { "Catalog": "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=organizor_catalog;Username=postgres;Password=<postgres-password>" } } Tenant PostgreSQL Settings ConnectionStringBuilder builds tenant and admin connection strings from the Postgres section. { "Postgres": { "Host": "localhost", "Port": "5432", "User": "postgres", "Password": "<postgres-password>" } } The admin connection uses the postgres database. Tenant connections use the tenant database name stored in the catalog. Keycloak The API requires Keycloak settings for two separate concerns: JWT validation uses Keycloak:Authority. Tenant onboarding uses the Keycloak admin client settings to create tenant groups, assign roles, create/update tenant website clients, and create the default tenant admin user. Example development shape: { "Keycloak": { "Authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev", "BaseUrl": "https://localhost:8443", "Realm": "organizor-dev", "AdminClientId": "organizor-admin", "AdminClientSecret": "<admin-client-secret>", "DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword": "<optional-local-only-password>" } } Authority must match the token issuer exactly. The local Keycloak container runs at https://localhost:8443, so tokens from the Blazor portal have issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. A mismatch between http and https is enough to make API authentication fail with 401 Unauthorized. The development API configures the Keycloak admin HttpClient to accept the local self-signed Keycloak certificate. This is development-only behavior and should not be used for production identity-provider calls. Store client secrets in user secrets, environment variables, or deployment secrets rather than committing them to source. Outside Development, the API refuses to start when Keycloak authority/base URL are missing, non-HTTPS, or loopback URLs. It also requires Keycloak:Realm, Keycloak:AdminClientId, and Keycloak:AdminClientSecret. Keycloak:DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword is optional. When omitted, onboarding generates a temporary password for the default {slug}-admin user. Do not configure development passwords such as ChangeMe123! or Admin123! outside Development. Portal UI The Blazor WebAssembly portal uses Keycloak for OIDC login and calls the API with bearer tokens. Admin tenant management uses Radzen components and AdminTenantService over the named api HttpClient. The portal reads these values from wwwroot/appsettings.json or the matching environment-specific Blazor configuration file: Api:BaseUrl Keycloak:Authority Keycloak:ClientId Authentication:RedirectUri Authentication:PostLogoutRedirectUri Current local development endpoints: Setting Value Portal URL https://localhost:7025 Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Keycloak client ID organizor-ui Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback API base URL https://localhost:7184 These values must stay aligned with the organizor-ui client redirect URIs and web origins in Keycloak. Quartz Quartz uses the Catalog connection string for its persistent store. The same catalog database stores tenant records and Quartz scheduler tables. The API registration configures: PostgreSQL-backed Quartz persistence; Newtonsoft JSON serialization for persisted job data; clustering support; hosted service startup for Quartz background processing. Tenant job scheduling is not enabled on application startup yet. TenantJobScheduler is available for future real tenant jobs, but the startup scheduling block is currently commented out until those jobs exist. Logging Serilog is configured in appsettings.json. Current sinks: console; rolling file logs under logs/log-.txt. Log output includes tenant and request correlation properties when available: Id; Slug; DatabaseName; CorrelationId. CORS The API selects a CORS policy by environment: DevCors in development allows any origin, header, and method. ProdCors outside development dynamically allows origins from active tenant website configuration in the catalog. Production CORS uses tenant auth.webOrigins values and the origin of website.baseUrl as the allow-list source. Wildcards, malformed origins, URL fragments, non-origin webOrigins, and non-local HTTP origins are rejected. CORS is not authorization; bearer tokens, role policies, tenant resolution, and tenant access checks still enforce API access. OpenAPI and Scalar OpenAPI and Scalar endpoints are mapped only in development. This keeps the production surface smaller while retaining local API exploration during development.

articles/database-provisioning.html.title: Database Provisioning | Organizor
articles/database-provisioning.html.summary: Database Provisioning Organizor uses one catalog database and one PostgreSQL database per tenant. Catalog Database CatalogDbContext stores tenant records in the tenants table and tenant plan definitions in the tenant_plans table. Important constraints: Field Constraint Name Required, max length 200. Slug Required, max length 100, unique index. DatabaseName Required, max length 200. PlanKey Required, max length 100, defaults to starter, references tenant_plans.key. Features Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. Settings Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. IsDeleted Required, defaults to false. DeletionReason Optional, max length 500. Important tenant_plans constraints: Field Constraint Key Required, max length 100, primary key. Name Required, max length 200. Description Optional, max length 500. Features Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. Settings Required PostgreSQL jsonb, defaults to {}. IsActive Required, defaults to true. SortOrder Required, defaults to 0. CreatedAt Required UTC timestamp. The tenant-config migration inserts a minimal starter plan row before adding the tenant plan foreign key. This keeps existing tenants migratable because their new PlanKey defaults to starter. After migrations are applied, startup seeding idempotently creates or updates the initial tenant plans: Plan key Purpose starter Default plan for new tenants with conservative limits. pro Larger customer plan with higher limits and more enabled features. The seed data is managed in SeedCatalogDbAsync. It runs after CatalogDbContext migrations so it can enrich the minimal migration-created starter row and add pro. Manual verification after startup: select key, name, features, settings from tenant_plans where key in ('starter', 'pro') order by sort_order; Creating or onboarding a tenant without explicit plan selection should leave tenants.plan_key set to starter. On startup, the API checks whether the catalog database exists, creates it when needed, and applies catalog migrations. The full tenant onboarding workflow is documented in Internal Operations. Database provisioning is one part of that workflow; Keycloak tenant access is provisioned before the tenant database is created. Tenant Database Naming Tenant databases use: organizor_tenant_{slug} Example: organizor_tenant_acme Slugs are normalized to lowercase before tenant records are written. PostgreSQL Requirements The configured PostgreSQL user must be able to: connect to the admin postgres database; create tenant databases; drop tenant databases during hard deletion; create extensions in tenant databases. Tenant database creation currently uses: CREATE DATABASE "{databaseName}" OWNER = postgres ENCODING = 'UTF8'; Each tenant database is initialized with: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto"; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "citext"; Hard deletion uses: DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{databaseName}" WITH (FORCE); Migration Flow TenantMigrator builds a tenant-specific connection string, checks pending migrations on OrganizorDbContext, applies them, and returns: Field Meaning Database Tenant database name. Success Whether migrations completed. AppliedMigrations Count of migrations pending before execution. Duration Migration runtime. Error Error message when migration fails. Onboarding and Cleanup During POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard, the database steps are: create the tenant database named organizor_tenant_{slug}; initialize required PostgreSQL extensions; apply pending OrganizorDbContext migrations; return success so the tenant can be marked Active. If the migration result fails or onboarding throws unexpectedly, the catalog tenant is marked Failed. During hard deletion, the tenant must already be soft-deleted. The hard-delete workflow drops the tenant database with DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ... WITH (FORCE) after Keycloak cleanup and then removes the catalog record.

articles/errors-and-observability.html.title: Errors and Observability | Organizor
articles/errors-and-observability.html.summary: Errors and Observability Correlation IDs Every request passes through CorrelationIdMiddleware. Clients can provide a correlation ID: X-Correlation-ID: request-123 If the header is missing, the API generates a GUID. The final value is returned in the response header: X-Correlation-ID: 2ad71e7a-13cb-4ef8-a4c7-f3a37ad9dc71 The same value is pushed into Serilog context as CorrelationId. Error Shape Unhandled exceptions are returned as RFC 7807-style problem details: { "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/500", "title": "An unexpected error occurred.", "status": 500, "detail": "Exception message", "instance": "/api/v1/tenants", "correlationId": "2ad71e7a-13cb-4ef8-a4c7-f3a37ad9dc71" } The response content type is: application/problem+json Note The current middleware includes exception messages in detail. Treat that as useful during development, but review it before exposing production environments. Tenant Resolution Errors Tenant-scoped requests require: X-Tenant-Slug: acme Missing tenant slug returns 400 Bad Request with a plain text response. Unknown tenant slug returns 404 Not Found with a plain text response. Log Context Serilog output is configured to include: Property Source CorrelationId Request header or generated GUID. Id Resolved tenant ID. Slug Resolved tenant slug. DatabaseName Tenant database selection when available. SourceContext Logger source in file logs.

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Organizor
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started For the full local topology, expected ports, startup order, and verification checklist, use Local Development. This page keeps the shorter first-run flow. Prerequisites .NET SDK 10. PostgreSQL available to the API. Keycloak available to the API. The repository includes a development Keycloak compose file. A catalog database connection string named Catalog. PostgreSQL server settings under the Postgres configuration section for tenant database creation and resolution. Keycloak bearer-token settings under the Keycloak configuration section. DocFX installed as a .NET tool when building documentation locally. Install DocFX if the docfx command is not available: dotnet tool install -g docfx Start the development Keycloak instance: docker compose up -d The compose file starts Keycloak at https://localhost:8443. Generate and trust the local certificate first if keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 does not exist. Configure the organizor-dev realm, clients, roles, and users as described in Keycloak Setup. Run the API From the repository root: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Development launch profiles expose: Profile URL http http://localhost:5100 https https://localhost:7184 and http://localhost:5100 On startup the API: configures Serilog; registers catalog and tenant database services; registers application and infrastructure services; seeds or migrates the catalog database; maps controllers, health checks, OpenAPI, and Scalar in development. Development Endpoints Endpoint Purpose /health ASP.NET Core health checks. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document, available in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer, available in development. Example tenant catalog request: $token = "<organizor-admin JWT>" Invoke-RestMethod ` -Method Post ` -Uri "http://localhost:5100/api/v1/tenants" ` -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } ` -ContentType "application/json" ` -Body '{"name":"Acme","slug":"acme"}' POST /api/v1/tenants creates a catalog record only and requires an organizor-admin token. Use POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard when you also need tenant database and Keycloak provisioning. Run the Portal UI From the repository root: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile https The HTTPS profile exposes the portal at https://localhost:7025. The portal is configured to: authenticate against https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev; use the organizor-ui Keycloak client; receive login callbacks at https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback; call the API at https://localhost:7184. Build the Documentation From the repository root: docfx .\docs\docfx.json DocFX writes the generated site to docs/_site and generated C# type-reference metadata to docs/api. Both folders are ignored by git and can be rebuilt.

articles/internal-operations.html.title: Internal Operations | Organizor
articles/internal-operations.html.summary: Internal Operations This page documents internal routes and workflows for developers and operators. Onboard Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "authSettings": { "websiteBaseUrl": "https://acme.example.com", "loginRedirectUris": [ "https://acme.example.com/authentication/login-callback" ], "logoutRedirectUris": [ "https://acme.example.com" ], "webOrigins": [ "https://acme.example.com" ], "registrationRedirectUrl": "https://acme.example.com/register/complete" } } The onboarding flow: normalizes the slug to lowercase; validates and normalizes tenant website/auth URLs; generates auth.clientId as tenant-{slug}-web; stores website/auth settings in the catalog tenant settings JSON; creates a catalog tenant with Pending status; provisions Keycloak tenant groups under /tenants/{slug}; assigns tenant-admin to /tenants/{slug}/admins and tenant-user to /tenants/{slug}/users; creates or updates the tenant Keycloak public client from the centralized auth settings; creates a default tenant admin user named {slug}-admin with a temporary password of ChangeMe123!; creates the tenant database using organizor_tenant_{slug}; initializes PostgreSQL extensions; applies tenant migrations; marks the tenant Active on success or Failed on provisioning failure. URL validation rejects wildcards, requires absolute HTTPS URLs, and allows HTTP only for local development hosts such as localhost and 127.0.0.1. Web origins must be origins only. The generated Keycloak public client uses Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, client authentication off, direct access grants off, implicit flow off, service accounts off, and the validated redirect/web-origin settings from the onboarding request. It also gets a tenant-membership group mapper so tenant website tokens include the tenant claim. Example response: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme", "createdAt": "2026-06-09T10:30:00Z", "status": "Active", "failureReason": null, "isDeleted": false } Query Tenants For Administration GET /api/admin/tenants Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns all tenant catalog records, including soft-deleted tenants. This differs from GET /api/v1/tenants, which returns only non-deleted records. GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns one tenant by catalog ID, including soft-deleted records. These query endpoints are used by the portal tenant-management surface and are protected by the same RequireOrganizorAdminRole policy as lifecycle operations. Example response: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme", "createdAt": "2026-06-09T10:30:00Z", "status": "Active", "failureReason": null, "isDeleted": false } Tenant Config Administration GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns the effective config for one tenant. Effective config is resolved from the tenant's assigned plan defaults plus any tenant-level overrides. GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns only explicit tenant-level overrides. PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "planKey": "pro", "features": { "branding.customLogo": true }, "settings": { "limits": { "maxUsers": 25 } } } Override updates replace the tenant's full assigned plan key, feature override dictionary, and setting override dictionary. Omitted override keys are removed and inherited again from the assigned plan or system defaults. Tenant admins can view their own effective config through the tenant-scoped endpoint: GET /api/v1/tenant/config Authorization: Bearer <tenant-admin-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme This endpoint requires tenant access and the RequireTenantAdminRole policy. Tenant Plan Administration GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Returns available tenant plans and their default feature settings. PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Pro", "description": "Larger customer plan with higher limits and self-service registration.", "features": { "registration.selfService": true }, "settings": { "limits": { "maxUsers": 0, "maxCamps": 25 } }, "isActive": true, "sortOrder": 20 } Plan updates replace the plan's editable metadata, feature defaults, setting defaults, active state, and sort order. Existing tenant overrides remain intact, so tenants can continue to diverge from their plan where an override is set. Upgrade Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Runs pending migrations for the tenant database. Example response: { "database": "organizor_tenant_acme", "success": true, "appliedMigrations": 2, "duration": "00:00:01.2340000", "error": null } Soft Delete Tenant DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "reason": "Customer cancellation" } Soft deletion marks the tenant as deleted, stores deletion metadata, and sets status to Deleted. The tenant database is not dropped. Hard Delete Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Hard deletion requires the tenant to already be soft-deleted. It: deletes the default Keycloak admin user named {slug}-admin when it exists; deletes the Keycloak tenant group /tenants/{slug} when it exists; drops the tenant database; removes the catalog record. Keycloak cleanup tolerates missing groups or users so a partially-provisioned tenant can still be cleaned up. Portal Admin Tenant Control The Blazor portal exposes the tenant operations above through /admin/tenants for users with the organizor-admin role. The page uses AdminTenantService, which calls the same admin endpoints documented in this article. Operators can: view all tenants, including soft-deleted tenants; filter the catalog by name, slug, database, or status; onboard a new tenant; inspect effective tenant config; edit tenant config overrides; manage plan default settings from /admin/plans; run a tenant upgrade; soft-delete a tenant with a reason; hard-delete a tenant after it has been soft-deleted. The portal does not bypass API authorization. Each operation still requires a bearer token accepted by RequireOrganizorAdminRole. Scheduled Tenant Jobs Organizor is wired for Quartz recurring background work, but tenant job scheduling is not currently enabled on startup. Program.cs contains a commented-out scheduling block for future use. The scheduler: loads all tenants from the catalog database; creates a durable SyncTenantJob with job key sync-{tenantId} in the tenant-jobs group; stores TenantId and TenantSlug in the Quartz job data map; creates a trigger named sync-{tenantId}-trigger in the tenant-triggers group; schedules the job when it is new, or replaces and reschedules it when it already exists. Current trigger cadence: 0/10 * * * * ? That Quartz cron expression would run the tenant synchronization job every 10 seconds when scheduling is enabled. SyncTenantJob reads the tenant data from the job data map, sets ITenantContext, and then runs tenant-scoped work through OrganizorDbContext. The current implementation logs execution and contains placeholder synchronization work. Quartz persistence is stored in the catalog database and uses the PostgreSQL tables added by the AddQuartzTables migration. The API configures Quartz with the Catalog connection string, JSON serialization, and clustering enabled. Documentation Deployment The repository contains a GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/docfx-deploy.yml. On pushes to master, it: checks out this repository; installs DocFX; builds docs/docfx.json; checks out the public documentation repository; copies docs/_site into that repository; commits and pushes the generated documentation. The workflow uses the DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY secret to push to the public docs repository. Sitemap and Crawlers DocFX generates docs/_site/sitemap.xml from the build.sitemap.baseUrl value in docs/docfx.json. The documentation source includes robots.txt, which is copied into the generated site and points crawlers to the sitemap.

articles/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Organizor
articles/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Organizor is the backend API for managing tenant environments. It keeps tenant records in a central catalog database and provisions a separate PostgreSQL database for each tenant. The current implementation focuses on tenant lifecycle operations: creating tenant catalog records; onboarding tenants by creating a tenant database and applying migrations through internal operations; resolving tenant context for tenant-scoped requests; upgrading tenant databases by running migrations; soft-deleting tenants before hard deletion; exposing health checks, OpenAPI JSON, and Scalar endpoint exploration in development. Main Concepts Concept Description Tenant A customer or isolated workspace tracked by Id, Name, Slug, DatabaseName, lifecycle status, and deletion metadata. Catalog database Central PostgreSQL database that stores all tenant records. Tenant database PostgreSQL database named from the tenant slug, currently using the organizor_tenant_{slug} convention. Tenant resolution Middleware step that reads X-Tenant-Slug, loads the tenant, and stores the current tenant in ITenantContext. Provisioning workflow Infrastructure workflow that creates the tenant database and applies tenant migrations. Project Layout Project Responsibility Code7Dev.Organizor.Api ASP.NET Core host, controllers, DTOs, mappers, middleware, OpenAPI/Scalar, health checks, CORS, and logging setup. Code7Dev.Organizor.Application Tenant service contracts, tenant models, onboarding, lifecycle, upgrade, and catalog-facing application logic. Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain Tenant entity and TenantStatus enum. Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure EF Core contexts, repository implementation, PostgreSQL connection string building, database creation/deletion, migration, and tenant context storage. Documentation Boundaries The documentation is split into two intentionally different areas: Area Purpose Conceptual docs Explain behavior, workflows, configuration, security, local development, operations, and integration decisions. Generated API reference Lists C# namespaces, classes, interfaces, methods, and signatures generated from source. Do not use the generated reference to explain workflows or product behavior. Keep that content in the conceptual articles so it stays readable and can include context, examples, and operational guidance.

articles/keycloak-https.html.title: Keycloak HTTPS Setup | Organizor
articles/keycloak-https.html.summary: Keycloak HTTPS Setup The development Keycloak container runs over HTTPS at https://localhost:8443. The Blazor WebAssembly portal uses this endpoint for OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, and the API uses the same realm issuer when validating bearer tokens. Why HTTPS Is Required The portal runs as a browser application and should not mix HTTPS portal/API calls with HTTP identity-provider redirects. OIDC redirect URIs must match the portal origin exactly. Keycloak 24 runs with explicit hostname and HTTPS configuration when started in production mode. Local HTTPS keeps browser, API, and identity-provider behavior closer to production. Certificate The compose file mounts a PKCS#12 certificate from: keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 Generate a trusted local certificate with mkcert: mkcert -install mkcert -pkcs12 -p12-file .\keycloak\certs\keycloak.p12 localhost mkcert PKCS#12 files use a local keystore password. Put that password in .env as ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD so it is not committed. Keep generated certificates out of source control. If the certificate is missing or not trusted, Keycloak may fail to start or the browser may reject the login page. Docker Compose The Keycloak service uses production mode with an HTTPS keystore: keycloak: image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:24.0 command: - start - --hostname=localhost - --https-port=8443 - --https-key-store-file=/opt/keycloak/conf/keycloak.p12 - --https-key-store-password=${ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:?Set ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD in .env} volumes: - ./keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12:/opt/keycloak/conf/keycloak.p12 ports: - "8443:8443" Start or restart Keycloak from the repository root: docker compose down docker compose up -d Open the admin console at: https://localhost:8443 Development admin credentials are read from the untracked .env file: ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME / ORGANIZOR_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD Browser Trust Chrome and Edge normally trust the mkcert root certificate through the Windows certificate store after mkcert -install. If Edge still reports ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID, import the mkcert root certificate manually into Trusted Root Certification Authorities: %LOCALAPPDATA%\mkcert\rootCA.pem Then restart the browser. Expected Local Endpoints Component URL Keycloak https://localhost:8443 Keycloak realm issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Portal UI https://localhost:7025 API HTTPS profile https://localhost:7184 The portal and API must both use the HTTPS Keycloak authority. Tokens issued by https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev will not validate against an API configured for the old HTTP Keycloak endpoint. In local development, set both Keycloak:Authority and Keycloak:BaseUrl to HTTPS in API user secrets. API User Secrets For local development, verify the API user secrets use HTTPS: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:Authority" "https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:BaseUrl" "https://localhost:8443" --project Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Restart the API after changing these values. Running API processes keep the old configuration in memory. The development API accepts the local Keycloak certificate for admin-client calls. Browser trust is still required for portal login. Troubleshooting Symptom Likely cause Fix Keycloak does not start Missing keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 Generate the certificate with mkcert. Browser rejects Keycloak mkcert root CA is not trusted Run mkcert -install or import the root CA manually. Portal login redirects fail Keycloak client redirect URI does not include https://localhost:7025/* Update the organizor-ui client redirect URIs. API returns 401 for portal tokens API Keycloak:Authority still points to HTTP Set authority to https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev.

articles/keycloak-setup.html.title: Keycloak Setup | Organizor
articles/keycloak-setup.html.summary: Keycloak Setup This document describes the Keycloak configuration for the Organizor development environment. It includes realm setup, API/UI clients, tenant groups, claim mapping, user/role setup, and the admin-client permissions used by tenant onboarding. The local Keycloak container is expected to run over HTTPS at https://localhost:8443. See Keycloak HTTPS Setup before configuring clients. On first startup with an empty Keycloak database, Docker Compose imports docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json. This creates the organizor-dev realm, the three development clients, realm roles, the /tenants root group, and service-account permissions for backend provisioning. Client secrets are generated by Keycloak and must be copied into local user secrets or local HTTP-client environment files as needed. Normal docker compose up -d reuse does not re-import the realm and does not regenerate client secrets. docker compose down -v deletes the local Keycloak database volume; the next startup imports the realm again and generates new client secrets. After using down -v, copy the new organizor-admin client secret into API user secrets: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientSecret" "<client-secret>" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Realm Setup Open Keycloak Admin Console. Realm dropdown -> Create Realm. Name: organizor-dev. Save. API Client (organizor-api) Settings: Client type: OpenID Connect Client ID: organizor-api Name: Organizor API Required values: Client authentication: ON Authorization: OFF Standard flow: OFF Direct access grants: ON Implicit flow: OFF Service accounts roles: ON Credentials: Open the Credentials tab. Copy the Client Secret. Store it in development tooling that requests tokens. The API currently validates bearer tokens only; it does not read the client secret from application configuration. The client secret is only needed by tooling or services that request tokens with the client_credentials flow. The infrastructure Keycloak admin client uses the separate organizor-admin service-account client during tenant onboarding. Configure these application settings from that client: { "Keycloak": { "Authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev", "BaseUrl": "https://localhost:8443", "Realm": "organizor-dev", "AdminClientId": "organizor-admin", "AdminClientSecret": "<client-secret>" } } For tenant onboarding and hard deletion, the organizor-admin service account must be allowed to use the Keycloak Admin REST API. The development realm import assigns the required realm-management client roles for: reading groups and users; creating and deleting tenant groups; assigning realm roles to groups; creating the default tenant admin user; resetting the default tenant admin password; adding users to groups; deleting the default tenant admin user during hard deletion; reading, creating, updating, and deleting clients for per-tenant static website clients. UI Client (organizor-ui) Settings: Client type: OpenID Connect Client ID: organizor-ui Name: Organizor UI Required values: Client authentication: OFF Authorization: OFF Standard flow: ON Direct access grants: OFF Implicit flow: OFF Service accounts roles: OFF Development redirect URIs: https://localhost:7025/* https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback http://localhost:5080/* Web origins: https://localhost:7025 http://localhost:5080 Use * only for quick local testing. Explicit origins are preferable because they catch redirect and CORS mistakes earlier. Tenant onboarding must not mutate the central organizor-ui portal client. Static tenant websites receive their own generated public client instead, using tenant-{slug}-web as the client ID. Tenant Website Clients POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard creates or updates a tenant-specific public client for the tenant website. Client shape: Client ID: tenant-{slug}-web Client authentication: OFF Standard flow: ON PKCE method: S256 Direct access grants: OFF Implicit flow: OFF Service accounts: OFF Redirect URIs: onboarding loginRedirectUris Web origins: onboarding webOrigins, or website origin when omitted Post-logout redirect URIs: onboarding logoutRedirectUris Protocol mapper: tenant-membership Mapper type: Group Membership Token claim name: tenant Full group path: ON Add to access token, ID token, and userinfo: ON During hard deletion, Organizor deletes this tenant website client. Static websites can discover their public auth contract at: GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth The response includes the Keycloak authority, generated client id, PKCE flag, required scopes, tenant header name, tenant claim name, expected tenant roles, expected tenant group paths, redirect metadata, and public registration endpoint. Tenant Groups Tenant onboarding creates the group structure automatically when POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard is used. Manual setup is only needed for bootstrap or testing. Group structure: /tenants /tenants/acme /tenants/acme/users /tenants/acme/admins Each tenant has: /users group /admins group On onboarding, Organizor assigns: tenant-admin to /tenants/{slug}/admins; tenant-user to /tenants/{slug}/users. It also creates a default tenant admin user: Username: {slug}-admin Email: {slug}-admin@organizor.local Temporary password: generated during onboarding unless Keycloak:DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword is configured Group: /tenants/{slug}/admins During hard deletion, Organizor removes the tenant website client, removes the tenant group /tenants/{slug}, and deletes the default {slug}-admin user when it exists. Tenant Membership Claim Mapper Generated tenant website clients receive this mapper automatically during onboarding. Location: Clients -> organizor-api Client scopes -> organizor-api-dedicated Mappers -> Create Values: Name: tenant-membership Mapper type: Group Membership Token Claim Name: tenant Full group path: ON Add to ID token: ON Add to access token: ON Add to userinfo: ON User Setup Create these realm roles before assigning users: organizor-admin tenant-admin tenant-user Platform admin: Username: admin@organizor.dev Password: local development password stored outside git Assign realm role: organizor-admin No tenant groups assigned Tenant admin: Username: admin@acme.dev Password: local development password stored outside git Assign realm role: tenant-admin Assign group: /tenants/acme/admins Tenant user: Username: user@acme.dev Password: local development password stored outside git Assign realm role: tenant-user Assign group: /tenants/acme/users Token Testing Token endpoint: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev/protocol/openid-connect/token Expected role claim examples: { "realm_access": { "roles": ["organizor-admin"] }, "resource_access": { "organizor-api": { "roles": ["tenant-user"] } } } Example tenant claim: "tenant": ["/tenants/acme/admins"] Keycloak Architecture Diagram flowchart TD subgraph Realm["organizor-dev Realm"] APIClient["Client: organizor-api"] UIClient["Client: organizor-ui"] Groups["Tenant Groups"] Mapper["Claim Mapper: tenant-membership"] Users["Users + Roles"] end subgraph Backend["Organizor API (.NET)"] Auth["JWT Validation"] TenantAccess["Tenant Access Middleware"] Controllers["Controllers"] end subgraph Frontend["Organizor UI"] Login["OIDC Login Flow"] end UIClient --> Keycloak[(Keycloak Login UI)] Keycloak --> UIClient UIClient --> Backend APIClient --> Keycloak Keycloak --> APIClient Users --> Groups Groups --> Mapper Mapper --> Keycloak Backend --> Auth --> TenantAccess --> Controllers

articles/local-development.html.title: Local Development | Organizor
articles/local-development.html.summary:
Local Development This page is the canonical reference for running Organizor locally. Use it to confirm the expected ports, startup order, and how the Blazor portal, Keycloak, API, and databases fit together. Note Keep this page as the source of truth for local ports and startup order. Link here from other articles instead of duplicating endpoint tables. Local Topology flowchart LR Browser["Browser"] Portal["Portal UI
https://localhost:7025"] Keycloak["Keycloak
https://localhost:8443"] Api["Organizor API
https://localhost:7184"] CatalogDb["Catalog PostgreSQL"] TenantDb["Tenant PostgreSQL databases"] KeycloakDb["Keycloak PostgreSQL
Docker service"] Browser --> Portal Portal -->|OIDC login| Keycloak Portal -->|Bearer token API calls| Api Api -->|JWT issuer metadata| Keycloak Api --> CatalogDb Api --> TenantDb Keycloak --> KeycloakDb Ports And URLs Component URL Notes Portal UI https://localhost:7025 Blazor WebAssembly HTTPS launch profile. Portal UI HTTP http://localhost:5080 Development fallback profile. Prefer HTTPS for auth testing. Organizor API https://localhost:7184 API HTTPS launch profile used by the portal. Organizor API HTTP http://localhost:5100 Useful for direct local API calls without the portal. Keycloak https://localhost:8443 Docker Compose service with local HTTPS certificate. Keycloak realm issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Must match API Keycloak:Authority. Keycloak token endpoint https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev/protocol/openid-connect/token Used for manual token testing. Required Local Configuration Copy .env.example to .env and fill the local Keycloak container credentials before running Docker Compose. Keep .env untracked. The API needs: a ConnectionStrings:Catalog connection string; Postgres settings for tenant database creation and resolution; Keycloak:Authority set to https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev; Keycloak:BaseUrl set to https://localhost:8443; Keycloak:Realm set to organizor-dev; Keycloak:AdminClientId set to organizor-admin; Keycloak:AdminClientSecret from the Keycloak organizor-admin client. optionally Keycloak:DefaultTenantAdminTemporaryPassword for predictable local-only tenant admin testing; omit it to generate a temporary password during onboarding. Warning The API authority must match the token issuer exactly. A token issued by https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev will not validate against any different scheme, host, port, or realm. The portal is currently configured to: use Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev; use Keycloak client ID organizor-ui; redirect login callbacks to https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback; call the API at https://localhost:7184. These portal values live in Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui/wwwroot/appsettings.json for local development and must be replaced with deployment URLs for server environments. Startup Order Generate or verify the Keycloak HTTPS certificate at keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12. Start Keycloak with Docker Compose. On an empty Keycloak database, Docker Compose imports docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json and creates the organizor-dev realm, clients, roles, /tenants root group, and service-account permissions. Start the API with the HTTPS launch profile. Start the portal with the HTTPS launch profile. Sign in through the portal and verify the API accepts the issued token. Commands Start Keycloak: Copy-Item .env.example .env docker compose up -d Reset local Keycloak only when you intentionally want a fresh realm import: docker compose down -v docker compose up -d docker compose down -v deletes the local Keycloak database volume. The next startup imports docker/keycloak/import/organizor-dev-realm.json again and Keycloak generates new client secrets. After a reset, copy the generated organizor-admin client secret from Keycloak and update API user secrets: dotnet user-secrets set "Keycloak:AdminClientSecret" "<client-secret>" --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Run the API: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj --launch-profile https Run the portal: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile https Build the documentation: docfx .\docs\docfx.json Generate a local documentation deploy key only when you need to update the GitHub DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY secret: New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\ssh ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "organizor-docs-deploy" -f .\ssh\organizor-docs-key The private key stays at ssh/organizor-docs-key and ssh/ is gitignored. Do not commit, copy into docs output, or delete this folder unless you are intentionally rotating the deploy key. Store the private key value in the GitHub Actions secret DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY, and add the public key ssh/organizor-docs-key.pub as a deploy key on the public documentation repository. Keycloak Client Requirements The organizor-ui client must allow the portal origin: Setting Value Valid redirect URI https://localhost:7025/* Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback Web origin https://localhost:7025 The organizor-admin client is used for API service-account operations during tenant onboarding and hard deletion. Its client secret must be available to the API through configuration or user secrets. Production Checklist Do not copy local wildcard origins, local certificates, or development secrets into deployed environments. Production should use real HTTPS certificates, explicit origins, and managed secret storage. Verification Checklist Use this checklist when local authentication or API calls fail: Keycloak opens at https://localhost:8443 without a certificate warning. The API Keycloak:Authority exactly matches https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. The portal login callback is allowed by the organizor-ui client. The portal calls https://localhost:7184, not the API HTTP endpoint. The API HTTPS profile is running before logging in through the portal. The signed-in user has the expected realm roles and tenant groups. The portal user information panel shows the expected tenant, preferred_username, email, and groups claim values. Related Guides Keycloak HTTPS Setup explains certificate generation and browser trust. Keycloak Setup explains realm, client, role, group, and claim mapper configuration. Configuration documents API configuration sections. Portal UI Overview documents the Blazor portal responsibilities and integration points.

articles/localization.html.title: Localization | Organizor
articles/localization.html.summary: Localization Organizor provides multilingual support for error responses using a simple, predictable, API-friendly localization pipeline. Supported Languages Organizor currently supports: en - English (fallback) nl - Dutch Additional languages can be added by creating new resource files in the Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources folder. How Localization Works Localization is driven by the standard Accept-Language HTTP header. Example: Accept-Language: nl The API resolves the culture for the request and uses it to translate error messages. If a translation is missing, the system falls back to English (en). Key Principles Application services return error codes only, such as TENANT_NOT_FOUND. The API middleware maps those codes to localized resource strings. No hardcoded user-facing messages exist in the domain or application layers. Localization is deterministic and client-controlled. Culture Resolution Organizor uses the following resolution order: Accept-Language header. Fallback to English (en). This keeps behavior predictable and client-controlled. Error Code Translation Each error code corresponds to a resource key. Examples: TENANT_NOT_FOUND TENANT_ALREADY_EXISTS UNEXPECTED_ERROR These keys exist in: Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources/Shared.en.resx Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources/Shared.nl.resx The middleware retrieves the localized string and injects it into the RFC 7807 problem response. Example Request and Response Request: GET /api/v1/tenants/unknown Authorization: Bearer <token> Accept-Language: nl Response: { "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/404", "title": "Tenant niet gevonden", "status": 404, "error": "TENANT_NOT_FOUND", "correlationId": "abc123" } The error code remains stable and language-independent. The title is localized based on the request culture. Adding New Translations To add a new language: Create a new .resx file, for example Shared.fr.resx. Add the same error keys as in the English file. Provide translated values. Register the culture in AddApiLocalization. Restart the API.

articles/portal-overview.html.title: Portal UI Overview | Organizor
articles/portal-overview.html.summary: Portal UI Overview The Portal UI is the Blazor WebAssembly front end for Organizor. It handles Keycloak sign-in, role-based routing, platform administration, tenant administration, public registration testing, and authenticated API calls to the backend. This page reflects the issue 98 portal work completed after the last documentation update. Current Capabilities The portal currently supports: Keycloak OIDC login with the organizor-ui client. Role extraction from Keycloak realm roles and organizor-ui client roles. Automatic role-based routing after login. Separate admin and tenant shells. An admin dashboard route at /admin. Tenant administration at /admin/tenants for platform administrators. Tenant plan default management at /admin/plans. Tenant user management from active tenant rows for platform administrators. Tenant effective config inspection and override editing from /admin/tenants. Tenant-scoped user management at /tenant/users for tenant administrators. Tenant effective config at /tenant/config for tenant administrators. Tenant profile at /tenant/profile for tenant administrators and tenant users. Temporary public registration shell at /register for testing tenant-user self-registration. Logout through /logout or the shared logout button. Current-user display with username, email, display name, tenant claim, roles, Keycloak groups, and tenant website navigation when available. Tenant dashboard placeholder under /tenant. The /admin/tenants, /admin/plans, /admin/users, /tenant/users, /tenant/config, and /register pages are backed by real API routes. The /register page is intentionally a temporary shell for exercising the public registration endpoint until tenant-specific static websites provide their own registration UI. Technology Stack Blazor WebAssembly for client-side rendering. .NET 10 for the portal project. Keycloak for authentication using OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. Radzen.Blazor for the admin tenant grid, cards, forms, buttons, badges, alerts, and notifications. IHttpClientFactory plus a custom AuthorizationMessageHandler for API calls. Routes and Layouts Route Layout Required role Purpose / MainLayout none Entry page. Authenticated users are redirected by role. /admin AdminLayout organizor-admin Admin dashboard placeholder. /admin/tenants AdminLayout organizor-admin Tenant catalog and lifecycle management. /admin/plans AdminLayout organizor-admin Tenant plan default management. /admin/users?tenantId={id} AdminLayout organizor-admin Platform control-plane user management for one active tenant. /tenant TenantLayout tenant-admin Tenant dashboard placeholder. /tenant/users TenantLayout tenant-admin Tenant-scoped user management. /tenant/config TenantLayout tenant-admin Effective tenant configuration. /tenant/profile TenantLayout tenant-admin, tenant-user Read-only Keycloak-backed profile. /register PublicLayout none Temporary public tenant-user self-registration shell. /logout none authenticated user Redirects to the Blazor OIDC logout endpoint and returns to /. /authentication/* authentication page none Blazor WebAssembly OIDC endpoints. RoleRedirector is mounted globally in App.razor, but it only redirects from the neutral entry routes (/ and the login callback). It sends organizor-admin users to /admin, tenant-admin users to /tenant, and tenant-user users to /tenant/profile. It must not redirect when the user is already on a target area, otherwise the portal can reload-loop. Admin Tenant Management The admin tenant page uses Radzen components and the AdminTenantService client. It supports: loading all tenants including soft-deleted tenants; filtering tenants by name, slug, database name, or status; viewing active, deleted, and failed tenant counts; onboarding a tenant with name, slug, website base URL, login redirect URL, logout redirect URL, web origin, and optional registration redirect validation; upgrading a tenant database by running pending migrations; soft-deleting a tenant with an operator reason; hard-deleting a previously soft-deleted tenant. opening user management for active tenants. inspecting effective tenant config; editing tenant plan assignment and tenant-level overrides.
