The page calls these backend endpoints: UI action API endpoint Load tenants GET /api/admin/tenants Load one tenant GET /api/admin/tenants/{id} Onboard tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Upgrade tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Inspect effective config GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config Load tenant overrides GET /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Save tenant overrides PUT /api/admin/tenants/{id}/config-overrides Soft delete tenant DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Hard delete tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete All admin tenant operations require a valid bearer token with the organizor-admin role. Tenant onboarding stores website/auth settings in centralized tenant config so later tenant website and auth provisioning can use Organizor as the source of truth. Admin Plan Management The admin plans page uses AdminTenantService and supports: loading tenant plan definitions; editing plan name, description, active state, sort order, feature defaults, and settings defaults; saving plan changes through the admin plan API. The page calls these backend endpoints: UI action API endpoint Load plans GET /api/admin/tenant-plans Save plan defaults PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Plan keys are intentionally immutable. Admin User Management The tenant catalog page is the entry point for platform tenant-user management. Platform administrators open users from an active tenant row, which navigates to /admin/users?tenantId={id}. The admin users page manages only that tenant's Keycloak users. It can create users, list users, toggle enabled state, delete users, and assign tenant roles within the selected tenant. The admin sidebar does not expose /admin/users as a standalone global directory. /admin/users without a valid active tenant id redirects to /admin/tenants. The page calls the admin user-management API through AdminTenantService. All operations require organizor-admin. Tenant User Management Tenant administrators can open /tenant/users to manage users for their own tenant. The page uses the tenant claim from the authenticated user; ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler adds X-Tenant-Slug to tenant-scoped requests. Regular tenant-user accounts do not see the tenant user-management route. Tenant Config Page Tenant admins can open /tenant/config. The page calls GET /api/v1/tenant/config through TenantConfigService. ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler adds X-Tenant-Slug from the authenticated user's tenant claim. Regular tenant-user accounts should not see tenant configuration in the portal. Their default redirect target is /tenant/profile. Tenant Profile Page Tenant admins and regular tenant users can open /tenant/profile. The page shows read-only Keycloak-backed identity data: display name, email, username, tenant, roles, and groups. Tenant configuration was intentionally removed from the profile page. The password-change action starts the controlled backend flow. Profile update allows only first name and last name edits. Security options remain a disabled placeholder. The account-action strategy is Organizor-mediated and Keycloak-completed. Password-change initiation uses POST /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/change-password, which passes through Organizor authorization and tenant-access checks before setting Keycloak UPDATE_PASSWORD for the authenticated user. After the action starts, the portal tells the user to sign out and sign in again to complete the Keycloak password update. The portal does not collect new passwords and does not expose a direct Keycloak account-console link to regular tenant users or tenant admins. Profile update uses PUT /api/v1/tenant/account-actions/profile, which passes through the same current-user tenant checks and writes only Keycloak firstName and lastName. The portal does not expose username, email, role, group, tenant membership, credential, enabled-state, required-action, or arbitrary-attribute editing from the current-user profile page. Public Registration Shell The /register page is a temporary public shell for exercising tenant-user self-registration. It posts to POST /api/public/register through PublicRegistrationService. The long-term model is that tenant-specific static websites own their registration UI and call the public API contract directly. This keeps tenant branding and UX independent from the Organizor portal. Tenant rows expose the catalog and lifecycle fields used by the UI: Field Use id Action target for upgrade and delete calls. name, slug, databaseName Catalog display and search. createdAt Created timestamp shown in local time. status Lifecycle state used for badges and failed counts. failureReason Failure detail shown below the tenant name when present. isDeleted Controls deleted badge state and whether hard delete is available. Authentication Flow The Portal UI uses: OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE; Keycloak as the identity provider; access tokens for API calls; Blazor AuthenticationState for role and user context; KeycloakClaimsPrincipalFactory to promote Keycloak roles into Blazor role claims. tenant group-membership claims emitted by the organizor-ui client mapper created during tenant onboarding. Current local configuration: Setting Value Portal origin https://localhost:7025 Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Keycloak client organizor-ui Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback Logout callback https://localhost:7025/ API base URL https://localhost:7184 The API Keycloak:Authority must match the token issuer exactly. A portal token issued by https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev will fail API validation if the API is configured for http://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. API Integration The portal uses a named HttpClient called api with base address https://localhost:7184 for authenticated calls. It uses public-api for anonymous public contract calls such as resolving the current tenant website link. ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler: configures the authorized API URL; requests the OIDC scopes used by the portal; attaches bearer tokens to API requests; adds X-Tenant-Slug when UserContextService can resolve a tenant claim. CurrentUserPanel resolves the authenticated user's tenant website through GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth and shows Back to Website only when the returned contract contains a website URL. The handler is attached with .AddHttpMessageHandler<ApiAuthorizationMessageHandler>() and configured once in its constructor. Do not configure the same AuthorizationMessageHandler instance more than once; Blazor will throw a handler already configured error. Summary The portal now supports tenant lifecycle operations, tenant plan defaults, tenant-level config overrides, platform tenant-user management, tenant-admin user management, tenant-admin config inspection, tenant profile display, and public registration testing.

articles/role-based-authorization.html.title: Role-Based Authorization | Organizor
articles/role-based-authorization.html.summary: Role-Based Authorization Overview The API authorizes requests with ASP.NET Core policies backed by Keycloak roles. Authentication validates the JWT first, tenant access middleware enforces tenant membership next, and endpoint authorization policies run after that. Roles Role Purpose organizor-admin Platform administrator. Can manage tenants and call admin operations. tenant-admin Tenant administrator. Can use tenant-aware application endpoints and tenant catalog reads. tenant-user Tenant member. Can use shared tenant-aware application endpoints and tenant catalog reads. JWT Role Sources The API maps these Keycloak claim shapes to ASP.NET Core role claims: { "realm_access": { "roles": ["organizor-admin"] }, "resource_access": { "organizor-api": { "roles": ["tenant-user"] } } } Only client roles under resource_access.organizor-api.roles are promoted. Roles for other clients, such as account, are ignored for API authorization. Policies Policy Accepted roles RequireOrganizorAdminRole organizor-admin RequireTenantUserRole organizor-admin, tenant-admin, tenant-user RequireTenantAdminRole organizor-admin, tenant-admin Use policies for new endpoints unless the endpoint is intentionally authentication-only. [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.RequireOrganizorAdminRole)] Current Endpoint Enforcement Endpoint area Policy /api/admin/tenants/* RequireOrganizorAdminRole /api/admin/tenant-plans/* RequireOrganizorAdminRole POST /api/v1/tenants RequireOrganizorAdminRole GET /api/v1/tenants RequireTenantUserRole GET /api/v1/tenants/{slug} RequireTenantUserRole GET /api/v1/tenant/config RequireTenantAdminRole POST /api/public/register anonymous GET /api/auth/whoami authenticated user only Tenant Interaction Role checks do not replace tenant checks. For tenant-scoped routes, a user must pass both: Tenant authorization in TenantAccessMiddleware. Endpoint role or policy authorization in ASP.NET Core. This means a tenant-user token for acme is still denied when it sends X-Tenant-Slug: contoso. Assigning Roles in Keycloak Realm roles are assigned from the user details screen: Open Keycloak Admin Console. Select the organizor-dev realm. Open Users and select the user. Open Role mapping. Assign one of organizor-admin, tenant-admin, or tenant-user. Client roles can also be assigned under the organizor-api client. If client roles are used, verify they appear in resource_access.organizor-api.roles. Test Matrix Scenario Expected organizor-admin calls /api/admin/tenants Allowed tenant-user calls /api/admin/tenants 403 Forbidden tenant-admin calls GET /api/v1/tenants Allowed tenant-user calls GET /api/v1/tenants Allowed tenant-user calls GET /api/v1/tenant/config for their tenant 403 Forbidden anonymous user calls POST /api/public/register for an active tenant with registration enabled Allowed tenant-user calls /api/admin/tenant-plans 403 Forbidden Token has no Organizor role and calls protected endpoint 403 Forbidden Valid role with wrong tenant slug on tenant-scoped route 403 Forbidden

articles/security.html.title: Security | Organizor
articles/security.html.summary: Security CORS Development CORS allows any origin, method, and header. Production CORS currently uses ProdCors, but no production origins are configured in code. Add explicit origins before relying on browser clients in production. Internal Admin Routes Routes under /api/admin/tenants and /api/admin/tenant-plans are internal operations routes. They perform provisioning, upgrades, soft deletion, hard deletion, effective-config reads, tenant override edits, and plan default edits. These endpoints require the RequireOrganizorAdminRole policy. Only tokens with the organizor-admin role can call them. Config override and plan default edits should be treated as privileged changes. They can affect tenant-visible limits and feature availability without changing tenant database data. Error Detail Unhandled exceptions currently include ex.Message in problem details. This is useful for internal development and AI-assisted debugging, but it may expose sensitive implementation details in production. Tenant Resolution Tenant-scoped routes depend on X-Tenant-Slug. GET /api/v1/tenant/config is tenant-scoped, requires a tenant-admin role, and returns the effective config for the current tenant. Platform routes such as /api/v1/tenants, /api/admin, /health, /openapi, and /scalar skip tenant resolution. Destructive Operations Hard deletion drops the tenant database. The service requires a tenant to be soft-deleted before hard deletion, which protects active tenants from immediate physical removal.

articles/spec-driven-development.html.title: Spec-Driven Development | Organizor
articles/spec-driven-development.html.summary: Spec-Driven Development Organizor uses Spec-Driven Development for feature work. Accepted behavior is stored in repository specifications under spec/ so requirements, implementation, tests, and documentation are versioned with the code. Constitution Before feature work starts, read: brief.md tech-design.md roadmap.md rules.md workflow.md AGENTS.md the relevant feature files under spec/features/ These files define customer intent, architecture boundaries, implementation constraints, feature order, standing rules, workflow, and agent behavior. Feature Specs Each feature lives in spec/features/{feature-slug}/ and contains: File Purpose specification.md Defines behavior, scope, authorization, tenancy, persistence, API impact, acceptance criteria, and open questions. implementation.md Maps the spec to projects, layers, migrations, and rollback considerations. testing.md Defines automated and manual verification. documentation.md Defines DocFX, README, operator, and integration documentation updates. finalise.md Records completion checklist, verification results, residual risk, and follow-up work. Use spec/_templates/feature/ when starting a feature. GitHub GitHub issues and projects are useful for discussion, prioritization, and traceability. They do not replace repository specs. Pull requests should link the relevant feature spec and confirm that: code matches the accepted specification; tenant isolation was reviewed; authorization was reviewed; catalog and tenant database impact was reviewed; DocFX documentation was updated or marked not applicable; generated API reference files were not manually edited. Before a local commit is created, the agent should summarize the changed files or feature areas, verification performed, checks not run, and proposed commit message. The commit should wait for explicit approval. Engineering Standards Feature implementation must follow rules.md, including the repository's C#/.NET architecture and coding standards. Apply SOLID principles pragmatically: keep services cohesive, preserve dependency direction, expose clear contracts at layer boundaries, and avoid abstractions that do not protect a real boundary or improve testability. Drift Handling When code and spec disagree, update the spec first or stop for a decision. Do not silently implement behavior that is missing from the spec.

articles/tenancy.html.title: Tenancy | Organizor
articles/tenancy.html.summary: Tenancy Organizor uses catalog-driven, database-per-tenant tenancy. Tenant Catalog The catalog database stores tenant metadata through CatalogDbContext. Each tenant includes: Id; Name; Slug; DatabaseName; PlanKey; tenant feature overrides; tenant settings overrides; CreatedAt; Status; FailureReason; soft-delete metadata. The database name convention is organizor_tenant_{slug}. Slugs are normalized to lowercase before they are stored or used for lookups. Normal catalog reads exclude soft-deleted tenants. Repository methods can include soft-deleted records when an internal operation explicitly asks for them. Tenant Plans And Config Overrides Tenant plans are persisted in the catalog database through the tenant_plans table. A plan defines default feature flags and structured settings for tenants assigned to that plan. Each tenant stores: Field Purpose PlanKey Stable key of the selected plan, such as starter or pro. Features Tenant-level feature flag overrides stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. Settings Tenant-level structured setting overrides stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. Each plan stores: Field Purpose Key Stable plan identifier referenced by tenants. Name Human-readable plan name. Description Optional operator-facing description. Features Plan default feature flags stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. Settings Plan default structured settings stored as PostgreSQL jsonb. IsActive Whether the plan can be assigned. SortOrder Display ordering for future admin UI surfaces. CreatedAt UTC creation timestamp. The catalog migration creates a minimal starter plan before adding the tenant foreign key. This allows existing tenants to receive PlanKey = starter safely during migration. Full seed data for Starter and Pro is handled separately by the tenant-plan seeding work. Startup seeding keeps the initial plans available and idempotently updates their defaults: Plan key Name Intent starter Starter Default plan for new tenants with conservative limits. pro Pro Larger customer plan with higher limits and self-service registration. Initial feature keys: Feature Starter Pro camps.enabled true true branding.customLogo false true registration.selfService false true Initial settings: Setting Starter Pro limits.maxUsers 50 0 limits.maxCamps 3 25 registration.enabled false true registration.requiresApproval true false branding.theme default default limits.maxUsers = 0 means unlimited users for the assigned plan. The system default limits.maxUsers = 5 remains a fallback only; it is not the default sold plan limit. New tenants default to PlanKey = starter unless a later workflow explicitly allows a different plan to be supplied. Effective Tenant Config ITenantConfigResolver resolves the runtime configuration a tenant should receive. The resolver is registered in DI and can resolve by tenant id or tenant slug. Effective config is built in this order: SystemDefaults -> PlanDefaults -> TenantOverrides Later layers override earlier layers. The returned model contains: Field Purpose TenantId Catalog tenant identifier. TenantSlug Stable tenant slug. PlanKey Assigned plan key. PlanName Assigned plan name. Features Effective flat feature flag dictionary. Settings Effective structured JSON settings object. Feature merge rules: feature dictionaries are flat; plan defaults override system defaults by key; tenant overrides override plan defaults by key; missing keys do not remove earlier defaults. Settings merge rules: JSON objects are deep-merged; scalar values replace earlier scalar or object values; arrays replace earlier arrays and their contents are not merged; type conflicts are resolved by replacement from the later layer; empty dictionaries behave as empty layers; JSON null values are preserved as explicit override values when supplied by the stored JSON model. Failure behavior: Condition Result error code Tenant does not exist or is soft-deleted TENANT_NOT_FOUND Assigned plan key does not resolve TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND Assigned plan is inactive TENANT_PLAN_INACTIVE Tenant Config API Tenant-facing clients can fetch effective config for the current tenant: GET /api/v1/tenant/config Authorization: Bearer <tenant-admin-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme The route uses the tenant resolved from X-Tenant-Slug; the tenant id is not accepted in the URL for this endpoint. In the portal, this route is exposed only to tenant admins at /tenant/config. Regular tenant users are redirected to /tenant/profile. Platform administrators can inspect a tenant directly: GET /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/config Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Example response: { "tenantId": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "tenantSlug": "acme", "planKey": "pro", "planName": "Pro", "features": { "camps.enabled": true, "branding.customLogo": true, "registration.selfService": true }, "settings": { "limits": { "maxUsers": 0, "maxCamps": 25 }, "registration": { "enabled": true, "requiresApproval": false }, "branding": { "theme": "default" } } } Expected error behavior: Status Condition 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid bearer token. 403 Forbidden Authenticated caller does not satisfy the endpoint policy or tenant access check. 400 Bad Request Tenant-scoped route is missing X-Tenant-Slug. 404 Not Found Tenant, assigned plan, or active plan cannot be resolved. Manual verification: Seed starter and pro plans. Create or onboard a tenant assigned to pro. Add a tenant-level feature or setting override in the catalog. Call GET /api/v1/tenant/config with X-Tenant-Slug set to that tenant. Confirm the response contains system defaults, plan defaults, and tenant overrides with tenant overrides taking precedence. Tenant User Self-Registration Anonymous tenant-user registration is exposed through: POST /api/public/register The request body includes the tenant slug, username, email, and password. The endpoint does not use X-Tenant-Slug; tenant resolution for this operation comes from the submitted tenantSlug. The registration workflow: Resolves the tenant by slug and requires it to be active. Resolves the tenant's effective config. Verifies self-service registration is enabled and the user limit is not exceeded. Creates an enabled Keycloak user. Assigns the user to /tenants/{slug}/users. The portal /register page is a temporary shell for manual testing. Tenant-specific static websites are expected to provide their own branded registration UI later and call the same public API contract. Tenant Config Management Platform administrators can manage plan defaults and tenant-level overrides. Plan endpoints: GET /api/admin/tenant-plans GET /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} PUT /api/admin/tenant-plans/{planKey} Tenant override endpoints: GET /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/config-overrides PUT /api/admin/tenants/{tenantId}/config-overrides Plan keys are immutable. A plan update can change name, description, feature defaults, settings defaults, active state, and sort order. Tenant override updates can change: assigned planKey; tenant-level feature overrides; tenant-level settings overrides. Tenant override updates replace the full persisted override dictionaries. Omitted keys are removed from that tenant's overrides and inherited again from the assigned plan or system defaults. Validation rules: feature keys must be non-empty; setting keys must be non-empty; undefined JSON setting values are invalid; assigned plan keys must resolve to active plans; invalid config payloads return TENANT_CONFIG_INVALID; missing tenants return TENANT_NOT_FOUND; missing or inactive plans return TENANT_PLAN_NOT_FOUND or TENANT_PLAN_INACTIVE. Portal surfaces: /admin/plans lists and edits tenant plan defaults; /admin/tenants exposes each tenant's effective config and tenant-level override editor through the Config action. Manual verification: Open /admin/plans as an organizor-admin. Edit a plan feature default or setting default and save. Open /admin/tenants, choose a tenant assigned to that plan, and click Config. Confirm the effective config reflects the plan default change. Add a tenant feature or setting override and save. Confirm the effective preview refreshes and tenant override values take precedence. Tenant Statuses Status Meaning Pending Tenant exists in the catalog but provisioning is not complete. Active Tenant provisioning completed successfully. Upgrading Reserved for upgrade lifecycle state. Failed Provisioning failed or an unexpected onboarding error occurred. Deleted Tenant has been soft-deleted. Tenant Resolution TenantResolutionMiddleware resolves tenant context for tenant-scoped routes. It skips platform endpoints such as: /api/admin; /api/v1/tenants; /health; /scalar; /openapi; root and common static paths. For tenant-scoped requests, clients must send: X-Tenant-Slug: acme The middleware loads the tenant from the catalog and stores TenantInfo in ITenantContext. If the header is missing, the response is 400 Bad Request. If the slug does not match a catalog tenant, the response is 404 Not Found. Tenant Database Resolution OrganizorDbContext uses a fallback in-memory database when no tenant has been resolved. This supports startup, Scalar, migrations, and design-time tooling. When a tenant is resolved, PerTenantDbResolver loads the catalog tenant, builds a PostgreSQL connection string for that tenant database, and OrganizorDbContext uses that database. Tenant Onboarding Flow flowchart TD A[Onboard request] --> B[Create catalog tenant as Pending] B --> C[Store centralized website/auth settings] C --> D[Create Keycloak tenant groups] D --> E[Assign tenant roles to groups] E --> F[Create or update tenant public website client] F --> G[Create default tenant admin] G --> H[Create tenant database] H --> I[Apply tenant migrations] I --> J{Success?} J -->|Yes| K[Mark tenant Active] J -->|No| L[Mark tenant Failed] The preferred full tenant creation route is POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard. It creates the catalog record, stores centralized website/auth settings, provisions Keycloak tenant access, creates the tenant database, applies migrations, and marks the tenant Active only after the workflow succeeds. Onboarding accepts tenant website/auth settings for separate tenant UI projects: Field Purpose websiteBaseUrl Public tenant website base URL. loginRedirectUris OIDC login callback URLs allowed by Keycloak. logoutRedirectUris Post-logout redirect URLs allowed by Keycloak. webOrigins Browser origins allowed by the Keycloak public client. Defaults to the website origin when omitted. registrationRedirectUrl Optional tenant website URL used after registration flows. These values are stored in tenant settings under website and auth, so Organizor remains the source of truth. Organizor also stores a generated auth.clientId using the format tenant-{slug}-web and provisions that Keycloak public client during onboarding. The tenant public client is configured for Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, uses the configured login redirect URIs and web origins, stores the configured post-logout redirect URIs, and disables direct access grants, implicit flow, service accounts, and client authentication. Organizor also attaches a tenant-membership group mapper so tenant website tokens include the tenant claim used by API tenant authorization. POST /api/v1/tenants creates only the catalog record with Pending status. It does not create Keycloak groups or a tenant database. Hard deletion is intentionally guarded: the tenant must be soft-deleted before TenantLifecycleService runs the hard-delete workflow. That workflow removes the tenant Keycloak public client, removes the Keycloak tenant group and default admin user, drops the tenant database, and removes the catalog record.

articles/tenant-authorization.html.summary: Tenant Authorization Overview Tenant-scoped API routes require both a valid JWT and an X-Tenant-Slug header. The API resolves the header to a catalog tenant, validates that the JWT is allowed to use that tenant, then lets controller authorization policies run. Tenant Resolution Tenant-scoped routes must include: X-Tenant-Slug: acme The tenant resolution middleware skips platform and infrastructure routes, including: /api/admin /api/public /api/v1/tenants /api/auth /health /openapi /scalar /favicon /robots Resolution steps: Middleware reads X-Tenant-Slug. Middleware looks up the tenant in the catalog database. Middleware sets tenantContext.Current. Middleware logs tenant metadata. JWT Tenant Claim Tenant membership is represented by one or more tenant claims. The middleware accepts either direct slugs or Keycloak-style paths: { "tenant": ["/tenants/acme/admins", "/tenants/contoso/users"] } The slug is extracted from the segment after /tenants/. For /tenants/acme/admins, the effective tenant slug is acme. Static tenant websites discover the expected tenant header and claim names through GET /api/public/tenants/{slug}/auth. That endpoint is anonymous and bypasses tenant resolution; authenticated tenant-scoped calls still require X-Tenant-Slug. Enforcement Rules For tenant-scoped routes: Missing or invalid Authorization returns 401 Unauthorized when the endpoint requires [Authorize]. Missing endpoint roles such as tenant-user or tenant-admin returns 403 Forbidden. Missing X-Tenant-Slug returns 400 Bad Request. Unknown X-Tenant-Slug returns 404 Not Found. A JWT with tenant claims must include the same slug as X-Tenant-Slug. A JWT tenant/header mismatch returns 403 Forbidden. A JWT without tenant claims is treated as a platform superadmin token and bypasses tenant membership checks. The organizor-api service account, identified by client_id = organizor-api, bypasses tenant membership checks. Matching tenant JWTs are still checked through ITenantAccessService.UserHasAccessAsync(userId, tenantId). If ITenantAccessService denies access, the API returns 403 Forbidden. Middleware Chain flowchart TD A[Request] --> B[TenantResolutionMiddleware] B --> C[Authentication] C --> D[TenantAccessMiddleware] D --> E[Authorization Policies] E --> F[Controller] HTTP Test Matrix Scenario Authorization X-Tenant-Slug Expected Tenant token for acme calls acme tenant JWT acme Allowed if ITenantAccessService allows Tenant token for acme calls contoso tenant JWT contoso 403 Forbidden Superadmin token has no tenant claim superadmin JWT any valid slug Allowed Service account token client_id = organizor-api any valid slug Allowed Missing tenant header on tenant route valid JWT omitted 400 Bad Request Unknown tenant header on tenant route valid JWT unknown slug 404 Not Found Missing token on authorized route omitted valid slug 401 Unauthorized Missing endpoint role tenant JWT without required role valid slug 403 Forbidden ITenantAccessService denies matching user tenant JWT matching slug 403 Forbidden Sample Requests Tenant-scoped request: GET http://localhost:5100/api/some-tenant-scoped-route Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json Cross-tenant denial: GET http://localhost:5100/api/some-tenant-scoped-route Authorization: Bearer <token-with-tenant-acme> X-Tenant-Slug: contoso Accept: application/json Superadmin bypass: GET http://localhost:5100/api/some-tenant-scoped-route Authorization: Bearer <token-without-tenant-claim> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json

index.html.title: Organizor API | Organizor
index.html.summary:
Organizor API Organizor is a multi-tenant ASP.NET Core API for creating, provisioning, resolving, upgrading, and deleting tenant environments. Local Only The local development path uses HTTPS Keycloak at https://localhost:8443, the Blazor portal at https://localhost:7025, and the API at https://localhost:7184. Runtime Architecture flowchart LR Portal["Blazor Portal
https://localhost:7025"] Keycloak["Keycloak
OIDC + roles"] Api["Organizor API
tenant lifecycle"] Catalog["Catalog DB
tenant registry"] Tenants["Tenant DBs
database per tenant"] Portal -->|login + token| Keycloak Portal -->|Bearer token| Api Api -->|issuer metadata| Keycloak Api --> Catalog Api --> Tenants Note Conceptual docs explain behavior and workflows. The generated API reference is reserved for C# namespaces, types, methods, and signatures. Documentation Map Area Use it for Getting Started Running the API locally and building the documentation. Local Development Canonical local topology, ports, startup order, and verification checklist. Portal UI Blazor WebAssembly portal authentication and API integration. Architecture Understanding the API, application, domain, and infrastructure layers. Tenancy Tenant catalog, tenant resolution, provisioning, and database-per-tenant behavior. Public API Behavior Public tenant catalog routes, response shapes, status codes, and client examples. Errors and Observability Correlation IDs, error responses, and logging context. Database Provisioning Catalog database, tenant databases, PostgreSQL permissions, extensions, and migrations. Configuration Connection strings, PostgreSQL settings, logging, CORS, OpenAPI, and Scalar. Keycloak HTTPS Local trusted HTTPS setup for Keycloak. Security CORS, admin route exposure, error detail, and destructive operation notes. Internal Operations Admin routes, tenant onboarding, upgrades, deletion, documentation deployment, and sitemap output. Solution Structure Code7Dev.Organizor.Api hosts the HTTP API, middleware, OpenAPI/Scalar setup, health checks, CORS, and logging pipeline. Code7Dev.Organizor.Application contains tenant use cases and service contracts. Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain contains the tenant aggregate and lifecycle status. Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure contains EF Core persistence, PostgreSQL database provisioning, tenant database resolution, and migration support. Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui hosts the Blazor WebAssembly portal that authenticates with Keycloak and calls the API. Runtime Surface Endpoint Purpose /api/v1/tenants Public tenant catalog operations. /api/v1/tenant/config Tenant-scoped effective config for the current tenant. /api/admin/tenants Internal tenant onboarding, upgrades, deletion, effective config, and override operations. /api/admin/tenant-plans Internal tenant plan default management. /health Health checks. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer in development. Start with the overview, then use the public API behavior guide and internal operations guide for workflows. Use the generated API reference only when you need C# type and member signatures.
